title: "IPv6 on the Same Triangle"
---

# IPv6 on the Same Triangle

Same three routers as the forwarding lab. IPv6 only, so a missing `ipv6` line cannot hide behind a working IPv4 ping.

## Learning goals

By the end of this chapter you can:

- Address a /127 point-to-point and a /128 loopback
- Forward IPv6 on FRR and on cEOS
- Install one static IPv6 route on each
- Ping a loopback with an explicit source

## Plan

| Node | Loopback | Toward the next router |
|------|----------|------------------------|
| r-frr | 2001:db8:0::1/128 | 2001:db8:12::0/127 to cEOS, 2001:db8:13::0/127 to SR Linux |
| r-ceos | 2001:db8:0::2/128 | 2001:db8:12::1/127 and 2001:db8:23::0/127 |
| r-srl | 2001:db8:0::3/128 | 2001:db8:13::1/127 and 2001:db8:23::1/127 |

A /127 has two addresses, `::0` and `::1`. Use them as written.

## FRR

```text
interface lo
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:0::1/128
!
interface eth1
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:12::/127
!
interface eth2
 ipv6 address 2001:db8:13::/127
!
ipv6 route 2001:db8:0::2/128 2001:db8:12::1
ipv6 route 2001:db8:0::3/128 2001:db8:13::1
```

`2001:db8:12::/127` is the same as `2001:db8:12::0/127`.

## cEOS

```text
ipv6 unicast-routing
interface Loopback0
   ipv6 address 2001:db8:0::2/128
interface Ethernet1
   no switchport
   ipv6 address 2001:db8:12::1/127
interface Ethernet2
   no switchport
   ipv6 address 2001:db8:23::/127
ipv6 route 2001:db8:0::1/128 2001:db8:12::
ipv6 route 2001:db8:0::3/128 2001:db8:23::1
```

Without `ipv6 unicast-routing` the addresses exist and the router does not forward.

## SR Linux

Enable `ipv6 admin-state` on each subinterface and add the address beside the IPv4 block from the forwarding chapter, or instead of it. Static routes use the same next-hop-group shape with an IPv6 next hop. Bind `lo0.0` into the default network-instance.

## Verify

```bash
docker exec clab-ip6-r-frr vtysh -c "ping 2001:db8:0::2 source 2001:db8:0::1"
docker exec clab-ip6-r-ceos Cli -c "ping ipv6 2001:db8:0::1 source 2001:db8:0::2"
```

### Predict

- Both pings work after the statics exist.
- A neighbour ping of `2001:db8:12::1` from FRR works before any static route does.
- Removing `ipv6 unicast-routing` kills the far loopback ping and leaves the connected ping up.

## Drill

Add OSPFv3 on the FRR and cEOS link only (`ipv6 ospf6 area 0` on FRR, `ipv6 ospf area 0` on EOS) and delete the statics between those two. Leave SR Linux on statics. You should see one OSPFv3 neighbour and a remaining static for the SR Linux loopback.
